policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders 'And our rafters are firs' with a single plural noun and no textual note attached to it; the three notes on this verse are all classed alternative_rendering (houses / of cedar . . . of fir / cypresses) and bear on English wording, not on the reading here. The qere rahitenu and the ketiv rhytnw differ only in the he/heth of the consonantal spelling and yield the same word 'our rafters', so no ASV wording can distinguish them. Both readings remain compatible and the qere base fallback carries the projection.
